answers.answer: To choose from values, use {pick} with the texts after a colon, separated by pipes, such as {pick:a|b|c}. To get a number, use {random.number}: one input gives 1 up to that number, two inputs give the minimum up to the maximum, and an optional third input sets the step.
answers.quote: With two it is the minimum up to the maximum, and a third input is the step between possible numbers.

answers.answer: You need to know where helpers go: in the text of a command, event response, timer, pipeline, Discord notification or webhook. You also need the input syntax, which is a colon before the first input and a pipe before each next one. Helpers in text that viewers write work only when Viewer Templates is on in Features, and some helpers never work there. All of this is in the opening paragraphs.
answers.quote: You type them in the text of a command, an event response, a timer, a pipeline, a Discord notification or a webhook.

answers.answer: It worked when the helper is replaced by a value in the sent reply. It failed when the reply shows the helper exactly as typed, braces included. That happens with a missing or wrong input, or with an input given to a helper that takes none. To tell the forms apart: dotted number forms and named rolls reuse one value within a reply, while {random.number:100} written twice draws twice.
answers.quote: A helper with a missing or wrong input, such as a maximum below the minimum, does nothing: it prints exactly as you typed it, braces and all.

answers.answer: Choosing a supplied phrase uses {pick:phrase1|phrase2|phrase3}, which also never picks the same item twice in a row in the channel. A number within bounds uses {random.number:min|max}, for example {random.number:10|50}. The second form follows because two inputs mean a minimum and a maximum.
